title: Repository artifact storage and naming governance
purpose: Record design-only governance for artifact naming, directory compatibility, large artifact impact, and large proof artifact storage decision preparation without moving, deleting, pruning, rewriting, or migrating artifacts.

nonClaims: No Git LFS adoption is authorised.
No external artifact store adoption is authorised.
No readiness, staging, production, deployment, compliance, store, release, live-provider, or human-acceptance claim is made.

observedArtifactSizeSnapshot.scanType: working-tree artifact and evidence file size scan

largestObservedFiles.classification: proof evidence human review action record

observedArtifactSizeSnapshot.growthTrend: The current retained shape shows per-run growth dominated by proof-cockpit machine-run JSON, evidence-index projections, custody records, external-review bundle copies, and screenshots. Repeated machine runs add a roughly linear artifact footprint unless projection-only reuse, retention classes, or owner-approved storage changes are introduced.
observedArtifactSizeSnapshot.retentionRationale: Proof-cockpit machine runs, evidence indexes, custody records, and human-review action evidence are retained because generated reports are lower authority than raw evidence and accepted proof references must remain resolvable. Screenshot and bundle projections may be prunable only under an approved retention policy that preserves raw evidence and reference integrity.

gitObjectSizeSnapshot.scanType: read-only reachable Git object size audit across all history
gitObjectSizeSnapshot.largestReachableObjectPattern: The top reachable Git objects are proof-cockpit machine-run JSON blobs under artifacts/proof-cockpit/machine-runs. The top observed range was 6543567 bytes through 17322907 bytes.

ownershipRetentionAndSafeAction.retentionReason: Retained machine-run artifacts support accepted proof, evidence indexes, and chain-of-custody review. Generated reports remain lower authority than the retained run context.
ownershipRetentionAndSafeAction.safeNextAction: Do not delete, migrate, prune, or rewrite history. Continue with retention classification, manifest coverage, content-hash custody, and owner-approved storage policy before any storage change.

artifactNamingProposal.generatedSourceSeparation: Generated reports and projections must live under paths that identify them as generated or projected and must reference the raw evidence or custody record they summarize.
compatibilityStrategy: Do not move existing artifacts until validators, manifests, issue references, and generated bundle references are updated.
Introduce compatibility aliases or manifests before path migration.
Preserve old retained paths as historical evidence where accepted proof references already point to them.
Any migration must include a reference-resolution check before completion.
migrationRisks: generated reports appearing fresher than raw evidence
large diffs that obscure semantic changes
validatorExpectations: strict path component validation for future canonical paths
controlled values for environment, provider mode, proof family, freshness state, and retention class
historical path compatibility until migration is proven
failure on missing, stale, unknown, or unresolvable artifact references

currentLayout.role: raw and normalized evidence retained for proof, review, and audit references
retained proof-cockpit machine-run artifacts, screenshots, custody records, generated projections, and external-review bundle material
generated review projection derived from retained proof-cockpit run material and evidence references
review-supporting screenshot artifacts retained under the proof-cockpit run context

canonicalRoles.authorityExpectation: higher than generated reports and required when proof claims depend on collected evidence
retained proof support with explicit environment, provider mode, proof level, freshness, and custody context
lowest-authority projection that must reference raw evidence or retained proof artifacts
reference and integrity support for artifact chain-of-custody, not a semantic definition
review aid retained under a run context; not a standalone proof upgrade

migrationPrerequisites: reference-resolution inventory across evidence, artifacts, generated reports, docs, validators, and Linear references
compatibility manifest or alias strategy before any path move
validator updates before canonical path enforcement
content hash and custody continuity for moved artifacts
no deletion or pruning until retention class and owner approval are recorded
generated-report non-authority markers preserved after migration

generatedFileClasses.authorityBoundary: Generated reports are lowest authority and cannot override source authority, validators, or raw evidence.
External-review bundles are generated projections for review and must not appear fresher or more authoritative than their underlying run evidence.
Indexes support discovery and must resolve to retained evidence before supporting a proof claim.
Screenshots support review but do not upgrade proof status without the underlying run and evidence context.

sourceEvidenceReferencesRequired: raw evidence path or evidence id

skippableWhenRelevantInputsKnown.condition: The validator is not validating bundle projection correctness, all referenced raw evidence and retained run artifacts are unchanged, and the projection manifest hash or custody link is current.
The validator is not validating screenshot retention, UI review evidence, proof-cockpit machine QA output, or artifact-size policy, and a retained manifest records the screenshot path and hash.
The validator is checking semantic source authority or raw evidence rather than report projection output, and the report is marked as generated and lower authority.

mustScanWhen: artifact manifest, custody, retention, generated report, proof-cockpit, evidence, freshness, or artifact-size policy changed
raw evidence, retained proof artifact, or source reference changed
artifact relevance is unknown or ambiguous
manifest, hash, byte-size, freshness, environment, provider mode, or proof-level metadata is missing or mismatched
the command is a full evidence validation, full artifact validation, terminal proof refresh, or migration reference-resolution check
largeArtifactScanAvoidanceDesign.fullScanTrigger: Full scan is triggered on unknown relevance, missing manifest coverage, hash mismatch, stale or unknown freshness, provider or environment mismatch, retention-class change, generator change, evidence policy change, or explicit full validation command.
largeArtifactScanAvoidanceDesign.failClosedRule: A skipped large artifact cannot satisfy proof by itself. If the validator cannot prove the artifact is irrelevant to the current check, it must scan or fail closed.

benefits: large binary payloads can move out of normal Git object flow
risks: additional setup for agents and CI
possible audit friction if LFS pointers are not resolved

benefits: can support retention classes and access policy separately
risks: external access, retention, integrity, and availability risks
loss of self-contained audit context if custody is weak

benefits: small canonical manifests remain in Git while large projections or screenshots move only after approval
raw evidence and references can be preserved with content hashes
risks: more complex rollback and access rules

storageDecisionPreparation.recommendation: Keep accepted proof artifacts and custody records in Git for now. Prepare an owner decision for whether selected large screenshots, generated external-review projections, or repeated machine-run payloads should move to Git LFS or an external artifact store after integrity, access, retention, and reference-resolution controls exist.
storageDecisionPreparation.ownerApprovalRequirement: USF-853 remains the owner decision for storing large proof artifacts outside Git. This artifact does not decide or apply that change.
storageDecisionPreparation.rollbackPlan: Any future migration must preserve the original retained artifact or a content-addressed copy until validators prove every reference resolves. Rollback restores Git-tracked references, custody links, and manifests before closing the migration issue.
futureValidationExpectation: artifact integrity check by content hash
reference-resolution check across manifests, evidence envelopes, generated reports, Linear references, and documentation
access and availability check for non-Git storage
